evals.name: user-card-feature
evals.prompt: Create a user profile card feature in this Next.js app. It shows the user's avatar, name, and role, plus a delete button that calls an API. Follow the project's component architecture.
evals.expected_output: A feature module under features/<feature>/components/<name>/ with a .component.tsx view (zero inline className), a paired .hook.ts resolving props/handlers, a .type.ts, and reusable visual pieces promoted to /components/<module>/[name].ui.tsx and /layouts/.
assertions: The component view file contains no className attribute
A paired hook file resolves props and exposes handlers
Reusable visual elements are placed in /components/<module>/ as .ui.tsx or in /layouts/
No use of any, @ts-ignore, or non-null assertions

evals.name: split-growing-module
evals.prompt: This features/dashboard/utils/layoutModel.ts file has grown to handle bounds, collision, and grid math. Split it into a clean module.
evals.expected_output: A named folder with a public entrypoint (layoutModel.util.ts) and semantic subfiles (geometries/bounds.geometry.ts, collision.geometry.ts, grid.geometry.ts), no generic helper.ts/index.ts names.
assertions: Creates a named folder with one public entrypoint
Split files use semantic suffixes such as .geometry.ts
No generic file names like helper.ts, common.ts, or index.ts
